subject: Post-call: Marketly embeddings & rerank — action items and success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@marketly.com>, Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@marketly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Marketly embeddings & rerank — action items and success criteria

Hi Samantha / Tom — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Key pain points (as discussed)
- Relevance degradation as index grows: current top-k precision drops noticeably past ~50M vectors.
- Cost & latency spikes on peak hours (flash promotions) causing degraded UX.
- Fragmented stack: experiments on FAISS locally, production on Pinecone + ES for keyword fallback — inconsistent configs and quantization.

Current stack / scale you mentioned
- Production vector index: Pinecone (v2) for embeddings + Elasticsearch for keyword fallbacks.
- Approx index size: ~120M vectors, average dim=1536.
- Typical query pattern: synchronous user-facing rerank (topK 50) + nightly batch re-rank jobs for personalization.

Failure / success criteria you want to hit for a PoC
- 95th percentile latency for rerank (topK 50) < 120ms (user-facing).
- Sustained throughput: 150–250 qps during peak with graceful degradation.
- Cost target: move unit inference cost down by >= 30% vs current Pinecone baseline.
- Quality: maintain current MRR/AUC performance within 1–2% of baseline.

What Redwood will deliver / next steps
1) PoC proposal & scope sheet (attached: redwood-poc-scope.xlsx) with benchmarks we'll run and required data.
2) Request a sanitized sample set (10k–50k queries + documents) — Marketly to share sample export (attachment: marketly_sample_queries.csv or temporary S3 link).
3) Technical kickoff: schedule 60–90m session next week to align on test harness, metrics, and access.
4) Baseline run: Redwood will run a 7-day baseline (quantization + batching experiments) and share a perf/cost delta.

Questions / clarifications for you
- Can you confirm whether the Pinecone index currently stores float32 embeddings or a compressed quantized form?
- Are the nightly batch reranks windowed by user segment or global? Approx size per job?
- Any regulatory constraints around sending examples off-site?

Proposed times for kickoff (PDT) — pick one and we'll send invites:
- Tue 2026-10-13 09:00–10:30
- Wed 2026-10-14 11:00–12:30
- Thu 2026-10-15 14:00–15:30

If that all looks good I'll send the PoC doc and calendar invite. Thanks again — excited to see if we can tighten your tail latency and cost.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-poc-scope.xlsx (xlsx), marketly_sample_queries.csv (csv)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@marketly.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@marketly.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T15:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Marketly embeddings & rerank — action items and success criteria

Thanks Ben — appreciate the thorough summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Pinecone currently stores float32 vectors; we've been experimenting with 8-bit PQ locally but not in prod.
- Nightly batch reranks are per-region (NA / EU), each job touches ~5–6M queries/doc pairs and runs in rolling windows every 2 hours overnight.
- Peak synchronous traffic: bursts to ~250 qps, baseline ~110–140 qps. Most user queries are sub-100ms target, so the 95th p95 <120ms goal makes sense.
- We can provide a sanitized S3 link to a sample set (we'll redact PII) — attaching a small CSV of representative queries for now.

We are fine with the proposed PoC. Tue 10/13 9am works for our engineering + search team (Tom will join).

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Search & Relevance | Marketly
samantha.lee@marketly.com

Ben — quick internal note before we lock kickoff: 
- I'll prepare two benchmark configs: 1) high-precision route (float32, minimal quant) and 2) cost-optimized route (int8/4-bit PQ + batched kv-cache reuse). We'll include suggestions for continuous prefix caching for frequent queries.
- For ingestion, ask Marketly for a schema export (vector dim, metadata fields, TTLs). That will let us map the shard/replica plan.
- I'll also prototype a latency simulation for bursts to validate p95 under 250 qps with our batching heuristics.

I'll attach a short checklist in the kickoff invite.
